newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank rejects bad debt bailout - Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank rejects bad debt bailout - Kyodo.

text.p: Japan's Sakura Bank has turned down a last ditch attempt by a debt-ridden leasing company to bail itself out of its huge bad loans, Kyodo news agency reported on Saturday.

Sakura Bank rejected a rehabilitation plan submitted by the non-bank money lender Apollo Leasing Co on the grounds that getting the company on its feet again was an almost impossible task, Kyodo quoted a bank official as saying on Saturday.

"Sakura Bank believes that nonperforming assets at Apollo Leasing are so large that it is extremely hard to reconstruct it even if 50 percent of the debt is forgiven by creditor institutions," the official was quoted as saying.
Sakura Bank and Apollo Leasing Co officials were not available for comment on the report.

Apollo Leasing, set up in 1972, extended loans to real estate firms during the asset-inflation period in the late 1980s. But like many small and mid-sized financial institutions, the collapse of Japan's economic bubble sent it into a tailspin.
As of end-March 1996, the balance of debt at the leasing firm stood at 489.7 billion yen ($4.04 billion), Kyodo said.
Sakura Bank, one of Apollo's main creditors, has already written off most of the 82.7 billion yen ($683 million) owed by firm based in Sendai, 350 km (200 miles) northwest of Tokyo.

Apollo also owes Nippon Credit Bank 69.3 billion yen ($572 million) and agriculture-related financial institutions about 50 billion yen ($413 million), among a total of 114 creditor financial institutions.

The bailout plan, mapped out by Apollo Leasing itself, calls for creditor financial institutions to waive 50 percent of their balance of loans, with the remaining claims and debts to be written off by earning revenues from 50 billion yen ($413 million) worth of its performing assets, Kyodo said.
